sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant is in appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2. The occurrence of the accident and the liability of the Insurer to satisfy the compensation are not in dispute.
3. The Tribunal, on consideration of evidence, proceeded to award a sum of Rs.1,90,000/- as compensation.
In arriving at the said conclusion, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 20% to the whole body and has taken the notional income of the claimant at Rs.1,000/-.
4. The Doctor, who was examined, has stated that the claimant has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 60% and to the whole body at 30%.
Since the Doctor, who treated the claimant, has assessed the whole body disability at 30%, it would be appropriate to assess the same at 30%.

5. Since there is no evidence to establish the actual income of the claimant, it would be prudent and appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2016, would be Rs.9,500/-.
6. The Tribunal has taken the age of the claimant as 66 years based on the Aadhaar card.

In my view,
this determination of age cannot be found fault with.

7. As a consequence, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.1,71,000/- (Rs.9,500/- X 12 X 5 X 30%)
towards loss of future income.

8. The amount of Rs.80,000/- awarded towards pain and sufferings and Rs.30,000/- awarded towards food, nourishment, attendant, conveyance charges by the Tribunal, being just and proper,
are affirmed.
9. Since the notional income is now assessed at Rs.9,500/-, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.38,000/- (Rs.9,500 X 4 months) towards loss of income during laid up period.
